campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution to authorize a funding agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for a low-carbon transportation program supporting transit reliability and performance improvements. The agenda also referenced discussion related to pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a low-carbon transportation and operations program fund agreement with VTA for transit reliability and performance improvements
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine items like meeting minutes, vendor payments, and the Treasurer's Report, and considered draft responses to two county Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims processes and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II. The Council also took up a transportation impact fee study contract, forming a committee to look at alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and the city's continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on data transparency for utility rate calculations
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several infrastructure and housing items, including a roof replacement contract for the History Museum, an EV charging station project at the Maintenance Yard, and completion of the Woodland Library Patio Expansion. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street and reviewed two large residential condominium developments on First Street and on Sherwood/Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: History Museum roof replacement contract with Diablo Roofing, not-to-exceed $147,500 plus contingency
Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, or referring it to the Historical Commission for further study
Vesting Tentative Maps for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street and 33 condominium units at Sherwood and Acacia Avenues
Maintenance Yard EV Chargers construction contract with Bockmon & Woody Electric Co., not to exceed $363,220
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes from several August sessions, along with a handful of other business items. Substantive items included vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista, setting up new preferential and time-limited parking rules, and authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive services
Approval of minutes from multiple August 2026 Town Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the draft agenda for the upcoming September 15, 2026 meeting, including whether to add items or assign specific times to them. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record covering August 20-27, 2026, and a study session on financing tools that could support economic development infrastructure.
keyTopics: Planning of the September 15, 2026 draft meeting agenda, including possible new items and time assignments
Review of the City Clerk's public record for August 20-27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development
The September 8, 2026 meeting was cancelled

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 31, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to take care of some foundational business, including a team-building exercise and a briefing on open-meeting rules and how the committee operates. Members also began brainstorming ideas for their work plan for the upcoming fiscal year, 2026-27.
keyTopics: Team-building activity for committee members
Overview of the Brown Act and Robert's Rules of Order
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's role
Brainstorming session for the FY 2026-27 work plan

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session followed by a special meeting focused on a presentation. The public portion centered on an update to the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session discussion
CleanWater Program update presentation

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 1, 2026
cupertino.summary: This Cupertino City Council meeting was largely ceremonial, featuring several proclamations and recognitions rather than major policy decisions. The Council honored a resident's 100th birthday and recognized the city's Innovation & Technology Department, alongside proclamations for National Preparedness Month and National Hispanic Heritage Month.
keyTopics: Recognition of Bertha Smith's 100th birthday
Proclamation declaring September as National Preparedness Month
Proclamation recognizing September 15–October 15 as National Hispanic Heritage Month
Recognition of the Innovation & Technology Department's divisions (Applications, GIS, Infrastructure, Multimedia, and Administration)

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, with Boardmember Chahal joining remotely from India. The agenda primarily covered logistical details for participation, including remote access via Zoom and instructions for submitting written public comments in advance of the meeting.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format with in-person and remote participation options
Boardmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Instructions for submitting written public comment before the meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: This meeting was actually a session of the Successor Agency to Milpitas's former Redevelopment Agency, a separate body that handles winding down old redevelopment debts. The City Council, sitting as that agency's board, considered confirming which city officials hold official roles for the agency and a plan to issue new 2026 refunding bonds to replace older redevelopment-era debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing the sale and issuance of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Climate Action and Sustainability Committee reviewed a preliminary look at the city's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including so-called Scope 3 emissions (indirect emissions from sources like commuting or purchased goods). The committee also considered different approaches the city could take toward reaching its carbon neutrality goal and was asked to give feedback on which areas staff should study further.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 greenhouse gas inventory and Scope 3 emissions overview
Discussion of approaches to achieving the city's carbon neutrality goal
Committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis on carbon neutrality
